symptom: refresh catalog after one model edit spent about 3 s of 5 s on widget definitions (Windows, FactoryManagement): `Widget definitions: 0 new, 2 refreshed` on every run, and the widget docs regenerated each time.
cause: Three causes stacked. KeyboardShortcut.mpk and itvisors.KeyboardShortcut.mpk both derived KEYBOARDSHORTCUT and rewrote one .def.json in turn, so the refresh always found drift and regenerated docs (which re-ran the whole refresh). The editorConfig visibility extractor ran end-anchored regexps (`…$`) over everything before each hide call, quadratic in the file: 0.5 s for Maps' 400 KB editorConfig.js. And nothing recorded that widgets/ was unchanged, so every refresh re-read every .mpk.
insight: Profile before caching: the issue blamed unzipping, but parsing all 54 .mpk took 45 ms; one 400 KB file in the extractor took 535 ms. Go's regexp has no backward search, so a `$`-anchored pattern on a growing prefix scans the whole prefix every time; use a suffix scan. A name derived from an ID must be assigned over the whole set, and every consumer (defs, docs, catalog) must look up by ID, not re-derive the file name.
